title: Counseling
one_paragraph_synopsis: In this episode, Dwight reveals a new daycare center in the office building and initiates a boycott of the Steamtown Mall after being snubbed at a store, with Jim proposing a direct confrontation instead. Meanwhile, Michael reluctantly participates in counseling sessions with Toby, showing anger and resistance, while Pam deals with issues regarding her unpaid status as Office Administrator due to lost paperwork. Dwight also undergoes a transformation into a gentleman with the help of coworkers, and later seeks revenge at the snobby store by purchasing a wizard figurine. The episode ends with unresolved questions about the outcomes of these events.

main_threads.thread: Dwight's daycare center introduction and his boycott of the Steamtown Mall after being snubbed, with Jim suggesting a direct confrontation.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Why didn't I think of this before? Did you know that there is a daycare center opening right here in this building?
Dwight: Welcome to the Sesame Avenue Daycare Center for infants and toddlers.
Dwight: Boycott the Steamtown Mall! Everyone, you heard me! Cancel all of your business with the Steamtown Mall!
Dwight: I went to the store and I pressed the buzzer, and they looked right at me, and then they looked away.
Jim: Dwight, how about this? Instead of boycotting, you and I, together, go down to that store and we teach those snobs a lesson.
Dwight: Ok

main_threads.thread: Michael's reluctant and angry participation in counseling sessions with Toby, including filling out forms and reacting to evaluations.

evidence.snippet: Michael: This is the worst! You are the worst! I hate looking at your face! I wanna smash it!

main_threads.thread: Pam's unofficial status as Office Administrator due to lost paperwork and her efforts to resolve the issue.

evidence.snippet: Pam: A few months ago. I was talking to someone at corporate, who isn't there anymore, and I think the paperwork just got lost in the shuffle.

Pam: So weird that there is no paperwork.
